definitions.explanation: A technique in martial arts, especially judo, sumo, and wrestling, that involves throwing an opponent to the ground.

examples.japanese: {見事|みごと}な{投|な}げ{技|わざ}で{勝|か}った。
examples.english: He won with a splendid throwing technique.

examples.japanese: {柔道|じゅうどう}の{投|な}げ{技|わざ}を{練習|れんしゅう}する。
あの{力士|りきし}は{投|な}げ{技|わざ}が{得意|とくい}で、{相手|あいて}を{豪快|ごうかい}に{投|な}げ{飛|と}ばす。
examples.english: That sumo wrestler is good at throwing techniques and powerfully hurls his opponents.

notes:
FORMS:
{投|な}げる (to throw) + {技|わざ} (technique). The {技|わざ} suffix is used for various martial arts techniques.

USAGE:
Most commonly associated with {柔道|じゅうどう} (judo) and {相撲|すもう} (sumo), but also used in professional wrestling and other grappling arts.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {投|な}げ{技|わざ}をかける (to apply a throw)
- {投|な}げ{技|わざ}で{一本|いっぽん} (an ippon by throw in judo)
- {投|な}げ{技|わざ}が{得意|とくい} (to be good at throws)
- {大|おお}{外|そと}{刈|が}り (major outer reap — a specific {投|な}げ{技|わざ})

RELATED WORDS:
- {固|かた}め{技|わざ}: grappling/pinning technique
- {関節|かんせつ}{技|わざ}: joint lock technique
- {寝技|ねわざ}: ground technique
